page: Microsoft Azure E32-8s_v4 is a constrained-core, memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by a 2.6 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor (x86_64 architecture) configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core. A key characteristic of this configuration is the high memory-to-vCPU ratio: it provides 256.0 GB of system memory, which translates to 32.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB L3 cache, along with support for AVX-512 vector extensions (including AVX-512 VNNI) and AES instructions.

Benchmark results place the general compute and memory capabilities of the E32-8s_v4 squarely within the average performance category. The instance recorded a Geekbench multi-core score of 4779.0, a PassMark CPU score of 8655.33, and a PassMark memory score of 2635.49. In synthetic compute evaluations, stress-ng multi-core achieved 7444.34, while read-only large block memory throughput measured 45.36 GB/sec and write bandwidth reached 32.22 GB/sec. However, heavily parallelized compression showed lower relative throughput, with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falling into the bottom 25% (28.42 GB/sec), reflective of the lower core count constraint.

The instance does not include integrated local SSD storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached remote disks for persistent workloads. For specialized compute loads, small-model (135M) language inference shows baseline utility (126.65 generation tokens/sec), but larger LLM inference on CPUs drops significantly, with 7B parameter text generation scoring in the bottom 25% at 6.54 tokens/sec. Consequently, the hardware balance delivers solid cost efficiency for memory-heavy enterprise software with per-core licensing requirements, such as relational databases, in-memory caches, and enterprise analytics platforms.
description: Microsoft Azure E32-8s_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. It provides 256.0 GB of RAM, offering a high allocation of 32.0 GB per vCPU, designed for workloads constrained by database core licensing. The instance does not include local storage or hardware GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show balanced middle-tier results across general compute and memory tasks, registering a Geekbench multi-core score of 4779.0, PassMark CPU score of 8655.33, and Redis SET throughput of 7.06 million operations per second. Multi-threaded decompression and larger LLM CPU inference exhibit constrained performance due to the 8-vCPU ceiling. E32-8s_v4 is suited for large relational databases, in-memory caching systems, and enterprise data processing needing substantial memory per compute core.
